bottleneck: Differentiating stem cells into a desired cell type rarely yields a pure population: protocols produce mixtures of target cells, progenitors, and unwanted lineages. Contaminating undifferentiated cells carry teratoma risk, while wrong-lineage cells can cause arrhythmias in cardiac grafts or dyskinesia in neural ones. Purification by sorting is imperfect, adds cost, and loses precious cells, so every batch faces a trade-off between purity, yield, and safety that no protocol has fully resolved.
current_state: Improved small-molecule protocols and sorting raise purity, but no differentiation protocol is yet 100% efficient, and regulators scrutinize residual pluripotency closely in every application.

sources.title: Cell and gene therapy manufacturing: Challenges and Innovations in Scaling Up

title: Stem cell differentiation yields impure populations
why_it_blocks: Impurity is both a safety hazard (tumors, arrhythmia) and a manufacturing tax. Regenerative medicine cannot scale while every batch needs heroic purification to be safe, and impure grafts risk harming the patients they aim to heal.
